_meta.layer: Response coverage / operational prioritisation — North-East (Sylhet) 2022 flash floods
_meta.purpose: Coverage side of the de-confliction protocol: where the coordinated response was focused, to compare against modelled need (gap = need - coverage).
_meta.install: Copy this file to Geospatial/backend/data/coverage_bgd_2022.json, then load it in scenario/sylhet2022.py via a _load_coverage() helper and set ScenarioContext.coverage.

sources.name: Flash Floods Humanitarian Response Plan 2022 (UN Bangladesh Coordinated Appeal, Jul-Dec 2022)
sources.publisher: Humanitarian Coordination Task Team (HCTT) / UN Bangladesh / OCHA
sources.used_for: The nine affected districts and the five heavily-impacted priority districts; the US$58.4M appeal.

sources.name: GAP Analysis: North East Flash Flood Response 2022, NAWG
sources.used_for: Sectoral need-vs-response gap framing; affected-population breakdown; % submerged (Sunamganj 94%, Sylhet 84%).

sources.name: HCTT Monitoring Dashboard / 4W matrix (response partners and funding by sector)
sources.used_for: Sector-wise response presence and funding gap (referenced; granular per-org 4W counts live in this product as PDF/dashboard — see caveat).

sources.name: FFWC / MoDMR situation figures
sources.publisher: Flood Forecasting & Warning Centre; Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief, Bangladesh

_meta.method: Per-district coverage_score is a TRANSPARENT TIER MAP derived from the HCTT Flash Floods HRP 2022 geographic prioritisation: the five districts the HRP names as 'heavily impacted' (Sylhet, Sunamganj, Moulvibazar, Habiganj, Netrakona) are the focus of the coordinated response and scored 1.0; affected districts NOT in that priority set (e.g. Kishoreganj) are scored 0.4 ('secondary'). This captures where the plan concentrated capacity. It is then read against modelled need (exposed under-5 x vulnerability) to surface under-served districts.
_meta.caveat: coverage_score is a documented TIER mapping from the HRP's stated geographic prioritisation + the national funding gap (23.5% funded) — it is NOT a measured per-organisation 4W partner count. The granular 4W (organisations x sector x district) lives in the HCTT Monitoring Dashboard / 4W matrix as a PDF/dashboard and was not machine-readable at build time. To refine: transcribe the per-sector partner counts from the HCTT 4W matrix into each district's 'partners_by_sector' (left null here) and replace the tier score with normalised partner counts. Do NOT present the tier score as an organisation count.
_meta.coverage_scale: 0..1; 1.0 = HRP priority (heavily-impacted) district, 0.4 = affected secondary district. Higher = more response coverage.

national_funding.note: Even priority districts were severely underfunded — the whole appeal closed ~23.5% funded.

_meta.scope_note: Keys below use the pipeline's ADM2 shapeName spellings (e.g. 'Maulvibazar', 'Brahamanbaria') so they join the scenario context. De-confliction reasons over this WIDER affected region (the five HRP priority districts at coverage 1.0 plus the affected-secondary districts at 0.4) — that contrast is what surfaces under-served districts. Supply/Education stay clipped to the tight incident scope (SCENARIO_DISTRICTS).

Kishoreganj.note: Affected (one of the nine) but NOT in the HRP's five priority districts.

Brahamanbaria.note: Affected (Titas/Meghna spillover, one of the nine) but OUTSIDE the HRP's five priority districts, despite high modelled flood exposure — the clearest need-vs-coverage gap.

Sherpur.note: Affected secondary district, not in the HRP priority set; limited modelled exposure.

Mymensingh.note: Listed among affected districts; no cells clear the exposure gate in the modelled footprint, so it does not surface as a need gap.
